- Primary goal: integrate Redwood in a private way for your payments ML features (embeddings + reranker + structured tool-calling).
- Security asks: mTLS for all control-plane traffic, IP allowlist for inference egress, DNS resolution to internal endpoints, and audit logs retained for 1 year.

3) Technical follow-up from Lauren to outline SDK/auth patterns and routing (regional pinning + fallback).

Thanks Marissa 

this looks right. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Security prefers mTLS for control-plane and data-plane auth where possible. We will need a mutual TLS handshake with certs issued by our internal PKI.
- IP allowlist: we need the list of Redwood egress IPs for the Dedicated/private offering. We can provide an internal ticket for allowlist once we have the CIDR or specific IPs.
- DNS: our infra team requires DNS resolution to internal hostnames (no public DNS records for the VPC endpoint). We'll need to set up conditional forwarding.
- Egress: outbound traffic must go through our NAT gateway; we cannot have unexpected direct internet egress.

On the SDK/auth side 

our team will prefer a service-account-like flow (machine-to-machine) rather than manual API keys. Also want guidance on running embeddings locally vs calling hosted embedding endpoints for cost and privacy tradeoffs.

I've attached an internal sketch of our network topology (architecture-diagram.pdf). I can loop in infra owners if helpful. Timeline: target pilot by Dec 10 and production by Dec 20, but Sarah will confirm.

Hi Alex / Sarah 

thanks for the detail and the diagram. Below is a proposed technical approach and immediate asks from our infra/eng teams.

Proposed architecture (high level):
- Private connectivity: use a VPC endpoint (AWS Interface Endpoint / Azure Private Link equivalent) to terminate inbound traffic into your VPC. Redwood will expose an internal hostname (private DNS) that resolves inside your network.
- IP allowlist: we can provide a stable set of egress IPs for Dedicated/Private traffic. For Hosted+VPC-endpoint mode we recommend expect to rely on interface endpoints (no public egress required). We'll supply CIDRs for your allowlist ticket.
- Egress & DNS: ensure egress to Redwood control plane is permitted via your NAT; for service discovery we'll use conditional DNS forwarding to our internal FQDNs.
- mTLS: mutual TLS for both control and data planes. We'll provide a cert CSR flow and a short checklist (see attached mTLS-certs-requirements.xlsx). Reducing complexity: if your PKI can issue leaf certs for service accounts, we can rotate on your schedule.
- Auth/SDK pattern: recommend service-account JWTs + short-lived tokens for session auth; SDKs will handle automatic token refresh and mTLS handshake when configured with cert/private-key. We'll ship a sample in the SDK repo (quickstart for service-account + mTLS).
- Routing & fallbacks: support region pinning in the client config (region: us-west-2) and automatic fallback to a lower-tier region if health checks fail. Fallback will be opt-in for private deployments.
- Structured output / tool calling & reranker guidance:
  - Structured outputs: use explicit JSON schema enforcement in Redwood's structured output feature to reduce hallucination when invoking internal tools.
  - Embeddings & reranker: keep embeddings in a dedicated project with strict access controls; use local reranker (server-side) that pulls candidate embeddings from the upstream store and applies learned reranking model. We can provide a sample retraining prompt set and eval harness.

Immediate asks (for your infra team):
1) Confirm the internal PKI owner (who will sign CSR) and point of contact for cert exchange.
2) Provide the NAT egress CIDR/allowlist contact or portal ticket number.
3) Confirm whether conditional DNS forwarding is allowed to external vendor hostnames.
4) Share a preferred window for a 30-minute handoff meeting (we propose Tue Nov 30 or Wed Dec 1).

Attachments: architecture-diagram.pdf (annotated), mTLS-certs-requirements.xlsx (fields + example CSR).

If agreeable I'll create a short mutual action plan with owners and dates and share via HubSpot.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
